description: This entry covers Diagnosis as part of the fundamentals of plant pathology. In this field, fungal pathogens matters because rusts, smuts, and blights, the historically devastating group. It is taught at the Compounded level of the teaching ladder, building from first principles toward professional practice, with each concept defined before it is used.
overview: Plant Pathology is the field concerned with Plant diseases: the pathogens, pests, and disorders threatening crops and forests. Diagnosis belongs to its essential core. Concretely: Fungal pathogens — rusts, smuts, and blights, the historically devastating group. And Abiotic disorders — nutrient deficiency, drought, and pollution mimicking infections. Mastering this entry means being able to explain the topic in plain sentences, recognize it in real cases, and apply it alongside the neighboring ideas of the Compounded tier.
core_concepts: Fungal pathogens: rusts, smuts, and blights, the historically devastating group.
Abiotic disorders: nutrient deficiency, drought, and pollution mimicking infections.
key_laws: Disease triangle: no epidemic without all three vertices present.
Van der Plank's epidemic model: logistic growth of disease with apparent infection rate.
vocabulary: Fungicide: chemicals killing or suppressing fungi.
Sanitation: removing infected material to reduce inoculum.
methods: Diagnosis: isolating and identifying the causal agent with Koch's postulates adapted for plants.
history: Plant pathology was founded by de Bary's 1860s proof that fungi cause potato blight; the Irish famine showed the stakes. Resistant breeding, fungicides, and molecular diagnostics followed, and the field now guards global food security.
key_points: Fungal pathogens: rusts, smuts, and blights, the historically devastating group.
